name: Tomato Catsup No. 2
description: Historical recipe from The Whitehouse Cookbook (1887). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

ingredients.name: gallon of choice ripe tomatoes
ingredients.originalText: one gallon of choice ripe tomatoes

ingredients.name: small level teaspoonful of cayenne pepper
ingredients.originalText: a small level teaspoonful of cayenne pepper

ingredients.name: whole cloves
ingredients.originalText: half a tablespoonful of whole cloves

instructions.text: Cook one gallon of choice ripe tomatoes; strain them, and cook again until they become quite thick.

About fifteen minutes before taking up put into them a small level teaspoonful of cayenne pepper, one tablespoonful of mustard seed, half a tablespoonful of whole cloves, one tablespoonful of whole allspice, all tied in a thin muslin bag.
At the same time, add one heaping tablespoonful of sugar, and one teacupful of best vinegar and salt to suit the taste.
Seal up air-tight, either in bottles or jugs.

source.author: F.L. Gillette
source.originalInstructions:
1. Cook one gallon of choice ripe tomatoes; strain them, and cook again until they become quite thick.
2. About fifteen minutes before taking up put into them a small level teaspoonful of cayenne pepper, one tablespoonful of mustard seed, half a tablespoonful of whole cloves, one tablespoonful of whole allspice, all tied in a thin muslin bag.
3. At the same time, add one heaping tablespoonful of sugar, and one teacupful of best vinegar and salt to suit the taste.
4. Seal up air-tight, either in bottles or jugs.
